answer: In an agent marketplace trading timber, sable pelts, and plume ornaments, dispute votes are weighted by tokens locked in escrow for 90 days, rather than by account count. Splitting one deposit among a thousand fake agents gives the attacker no extra voting power. To outvote honest agents, the attacker must lock more tokens than they collectively hold in escrow, tying up that capital and bearing its price risk for the full lock period.
